rows.answer: Assuming "best" means on-time delivery rate on Delivered loads, with at least 20 delivered loads to be meaningful, the top carrier is Pioneer Carriers 98 LLC at 92.94% (158 of 170 on time). Big River Hauling Co. (92.82%, 195 loads), Eagle Transit 97 LLC (92.66%), Midsouth Freight LLC and Lone Star Lines 84 LLC (both 92.18%) follow closely. Across the 40 carriers with at least 20 delivered loads, the fleet average is 88.48%, and the weakest is at 46.3%. I can also rank by margin or claims if you want a different view of "best."
sql:
WITH d AS (
  SELECT l.carrier_id,
         COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
         SUM(CASE WHEN julianday(l.delivery_actual) <= julianday(l.delivery_appt) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS on_time_loads
  FROM loads l
  WHERE l.status = 'Delivered' AND l.delivery_actual IS NOT NULL AND l.delivery_appt IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY l.carrier_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
)
SELECT c.name AS carrier,
       d.delivered_loads,
       d.on_time_loads,
       ROUND(100.0 * d.on_time_loads / d.delivered_loads, 2) AS on_time_pct
FROM d
JOIN carriers c ON c.carrier_id = d.carrier_id
ORDER BY on_time_pct DESC, d.delivered_loads DESC
LIMIT 15

WITH d AS (
  SELECT l.carrier_id,
         COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
         SUM(CASE WHEN julianday(l.delivery_actual) <= julianday(l.delivery_appt) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS on_time_loads
  FROM loads l
  WHERE l.status = 'Delivered' AND l.delivery_actual IS NOT NULL AND l.delivery_appt IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY l.carrier_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS carriers_with_20_plus_delivered,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(on_time_loads) / SUM(delivered_loads), 2) AS fleet_on_time_pct,
       ROUND(MIN(100.0 * on_time_loads / delivered_loads), 2) AS worst_on_time_pct,
       ROUND(MAX(100.0 * on_time_loads / delivered_loads), 2) AS best_on_time_pct
FROM d
LIMIT 200

rows.answer: Assuming "lately" means the last six months by pickup date, margin held steady at about 14.5% from April through August, then fell to 13.81% in September. September's total margin was $546,905, the lowest of the period, and average margin per load dropped from about $262 to $246. September also had fewer delivered loads (2,222 versus roughly 2,320 in prior months), so the drop is both thinner margins and lower volume. Note that September's loads may not be fully delivered yet, which could skew these figures.
sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', pickup_actual) AS month,
       COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
       ROUND(SUM(shipper_rate), 2) AS total_revenue,
       ROUND(SUM(carrier_cost), 2) AS total_carrier_cost,
       ROUND(SUM(shipper_rate - carrier_cost), 2) AS total_margin,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(shipper_rate - carrier_cost) / SUM(shipper_rate), 2) AS margin_pct,
       ROUND(AVG(shipper_rate - carrier_cost), 2) AS avg_margin_per_load
FROM loads
WHERE status = 'Delivered'
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
LIMIT 200

rows.answer: The average transit time from actual pickup to actual delivery for the 497 delivered Memphis, TN to Atlanta, GA loads is 14.12 hours. Individual loads ranged from 7.13 to 44.05 hours.
sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
       ROUND(AVG((julianday(delivery_actual) - julianday(pickup_actual)) * 24), 2) AS avg_transit_hours,
       ROUND(MIN((julianday(delivery_actual) - julianday(pickup_actual)) * 24), 2) AS min_transit_hours,
       ROUND(MAX((julianday(delivery_actual) - julianday(pickup_actual)) * 24), 2) AS max_transit_hours
FROM loads
WHERE status = 'Delivered'
  AND origin_city = 'Memphis' AND origin_state = 'TN'
  AND dest_city = 'Atlanta' AND dest_state = 'GA'
  AND pickup_actual IS NOT NULL AND delivery_actual IS NOT NULL
LIMIT 200

rows.answer: Bluegrass Haulers LLC arrived late on 87 of its 162 delivered loads, a late rate of 53.7%. The count covers all loads with status Delivered, with no date filter, since the question didn't specify a period.
sql:
SELECT c.name, c.carrier_id, COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
SUM(CASE WHEN l.delivery_actual > l.delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_loads,
ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.delivery_actual > l.delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS late_pct
FROM loads l JOIN carriers c ON c.carrier_id = l.carrier_id
WHERE l.status = 'Delivered' AND c.name LIKE 'Bluegrass Haulers%'
GROUP BY c.name, c.carrier_id
LIMIT 200

rows.answer: I can't give you the dispatcher's name, phone, or email, since those are personal contact fields. For Bluegrass Haulers LLC (MC101554, DOT 2005502), 87 of 162 delivered loads were late, a late rate of 53.7%. You can look up their contact details in your carrier onboarding records or the carrier's MC/DOT listing, using those numbers. I can also break the late loads down by lane or month if that would help the call.
sql:
WITH c AS (SELECT carrier_id, name, mc_number, dot_number FROM carriers WHERE name = 'Bluegrass Haulers LLC'),
d AS (
  SELECT l.load_id, l.delivery_appt, l.delivery_actual
  FROM loads l JOIN c ON l.carrier_id = c.carrier_id
  WHERE l.status = 'Delivered'
)
SELECT c.name, c.mc_number, c.dot_number,
  COUNT(d.load_id) AS delivered_loads,
  SUM(CASE WHEN d.delivery_actual > d.delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_loads,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN d.delivery_actual > d.delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(d.load_id),0), 2) AS late_pct
FROM c LEFT JOIN d ON 1=1
GROUP BY c.name, c.mc_number, c.dot_number
LIMIT 200

Assuming "September 2026" means detention charges created in September, Harbor Foods DC - Atlanta (Atlanta, GA) had the most, with 10 charges totaling $2,343.75 (about $234.38 each). It was the only delivery facility with September detention charges linked through `loads.delivery_facility_id`, so charges on loads without a known delivery facility are not included.
sql:
SELECT f.facility_id, f.name, f.city, f.state,
       COUNT(a.accessorial_id) AS detention_charges,
       ROUND(SUM(a.amount), 2) AS detention_total,
       ROUND(AVG(a.amount), 2) AS avg_detention
FROM accessorials a
JOIN loads l ON l.load_id = a.load_id
JOIN facilities f ON f.facility_id = l.delivery_facility_id
WHERE a.type = 'Detention'
  AND strftime('%Y-%m', a.created_at) = '2026-09'
GROUP BY f.facility_id, f.name, f.city, f.state
ORDER BY detention_total DESC
LIMIT 10

sql:
SELECT f.facility_id, f.name, COUNT(a.accessorial_id) AS detention_charges, ROUND(SUM(a.amount), 2) AS total_amount
FROM accessorials a
JOIN loads l ON l.load_id = a.load_id
JOIN facilities f ON f.facility_id = l.delivery_facility_id

SELECT 'pickup' AS stop_side, COUNT(a.accessorial_id) AS detention_charges, ROUND(SUM(a.amount), 2) AS total_amount

WHERE a.type = 'Detention' AND l.delivery_facility_id = 10

Memphis, TN to Chicago, IL delivered loads by pickup month (linehaul margin = shipper_rate − carrier_cost):

| Pickup month | Delivered loads | Total margin | Margin % |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-04 | 45 | $10,289.58 | 13.88% |
| 2026-05 | 45 | $10,435.92 | 14.03% |
| 2026-06 | 44 | $10,263.04 | 14.21% |
| 2026-07 | 71 | $16,121.42 | 13.79% |
| 2026-08 | 58 | $13,455.52 | 14.06% |
| 2026-09 | 70 | -$7,546.34 | -6.52% |

April through August were steady at about 14% margin. September is the outlier: 70 loads produced a negative total margin, so carrier costs exceeded shipper rates on this lane that month. I haven't looked into the cause. It could be a rate or cost data issue, or real pricing problems, and it's worth checking before relying on September's numbers.
sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', pickup_actual) AS pickup_month,
       COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
       ROUND(SUM(shipper_rate - carrier_cost), 2) AS total_margin,
       ROUND(SUM(shipper_rate - carrier_cost) * 1.0 / SUM(shipper_rate), 4) AS margin_pct
FROM loads
WHERE status = 'Delivered'
  AND origin_city = 'Memphis' AND origin_state = 'TN'
  AND dest_city = 'Chicago' AND dest_state = 'IL'
GROUP BY pickup_month
ORDER BY pickup_month
LIMIT 200

rows.answer: Assuming "picked up in September" means `pickup_actual` falls in 2026-09, one lane had a negative total margin: **Memphis, TN → Chicago, IL**. Its 70 delivered loads lost **$7,546.34** in linehaul margin, a margin of -6.52%. No other lane was negative for the month.
sql:
WITH lanes AS (
  SELECT origin_city, origin_state, dest_city, dest_state,
         COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
         ROUND(SUM(shipper_rate - carrier_cost), 2) AS total_margin,
         ROUND(SUM(shipper_rate - carrier_cost) * 1.0 / SUM(shipper_rate) * 100, 2) AS margin_pct
  FROM loads
  WHERE status = 'Delivered'
    AND strftime('%Y-%m', pickup_actual) = '2026-09'
  GROUP BY origin_city, origin_state, dest_city, dest_state
)
SELECT *
FROM lanes
WHERE total_margin < 0
ORDER BY total_margin ASC
LIMIT 200

WITH sep AS (
  SELECT l.load_id, l.carrier_id, l.delivery_appt, l.delivery_actual
  FROM loads l
  WHERE l.status = 'Delivered'
    AND strftime('%Y-%m', l.pickup_actual) = '2026-09'
)
SELECT c.name AS carrier,
       COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.delivery_actual > s.delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_deliveries,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN s.delivery_actual > s.delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS late_pct

JOIN carriers c ON c.carrier_id = s.carrier_id
GROUP BY c.carrier_id, c.name
ORDER BY late_deliveries DESC, late_pct DESC

rows.answer: Late delivery rates on delivered loads, by delivery appointment month, were 9.92% in April, 11.13% in May, 10.23% in June, 10.07% in July, 9.87% in August, and 11.15% in September. September was the worst month, with 254 of 2,279 delivered loads late. The rate stayed between roughly 10% and 11% all six months. I excluded delivered loads with a missing appointment or actual delivery time.
sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', delivery_appt) AS appt_month,
       COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
       SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_actual > delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_loads,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_actual > delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS late_rate_pct
FROM loads
WHERE status = 'Delivered'
  AND delivery_appt IS NOT NULL AND delivery_actual IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY appt_month
ORDER BY appt_month
LIMIT 200

rows.answer: **779 of our 1,800 carriers (43.28%) carry less than $250,000 in cargo insurance.** This counts only carriers with a recorded cargo insurance limit below that threshold. Carriers with a missing limit are not included, so the true figure could be slightly higher.
sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS carriers_under_250k, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM carriers) AS total_carriers, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM carriers), 2) AS pct_under_250k FROM carriers WHERE cargo_insurance_limit < 250000
LIMIT 200

rows.answer: We spent **$22,407.29** on lumper fees across 91 lumper line items for loads picked up in September 2026. I matched loads by actual pickup date and counted only accessorials of type "Lumper."
sql:
SELECT a.type, COUNT(*) AS line_items, ROUND(SUM(a.amount), 2) AS total_amount
FROM accessorials a
JOIN loads l ON l.load_id = a.load_id
WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', l.pickup_actual) = '2026-09'
  AND LOWER(a.type) LIKE '%lumper%'
GROUP BY a.type
LIMIT 200

SELECT type, COUNT(*) AS line_items
FROM accessorials
GROUP BY type
ORDER BY line_items DESC
LIMIT 200

rows.answer: Delivered FTL loads earn a margin of about 14.3% to 14.6% across all three equipment types. Flatbed is highest at 14.55% (1,619 loads), Reefer is at 14.49% (2,935 loads), and Dry Van is lowest at 14.29% (6,886 loads). Margin is shipper rate minus carrier cost on linehaul only, and the spread between equipment types is small, under a third of a point.
sql:
SELECT equipment,
       COUNT(*) AS loads,
       ROUND(SUM(shipper_rate), 2) AS total_revenue,
       ROUND(SUM(shipper_rate - carrier_cost), 2) AS total_margin,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(shipper_rate - carrier_cost) / SUM(shipper_rate), 2) AS margin_pct
FROM loads
WHERE status = 'Delivered' AND mode = 'FTL'
GROUP BY equipment
ORDER BY margin_pct DESC
LIMIT 200

rows.answer: I can't change records, since this database is read-only, so the safety rating for Bluegrass Haulers LLC stays at Satisfactory. The data does back up the lateness concern: only 46.3% of their 162 delivered loads arrived on time, and 87 were late. Your team would need to make the rating change in the TMS through whoever maintains carrier records. I can also pull a breakdown of their late loads by lane or month if that helps the review.
sql:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT carrier_id, name, safety_rating FROM carriers WHERE name LIKE '%Bluegrass Haulers%'
)
SELECT c.name, c.safety_rating,
  COUNT(l.load_id) AS delivered_loads,
  SUM(CASE WHEN l.delivery_actual > l.delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_loads,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.delivery_actual <= l.delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(l.load_id), 2) AS on_time_pct
FROM c
LEFT JOIN loads l ON l.carrier_id = c.carrier_id AND l.status = 'Delivered'
GROUP BY c.name, c.safety_rating
LIMIT 200

rows.answer: Bluegrass Haulers LLC has the worst on-time delivery rate among carriers with at least 50 delivered loads, at 46.3% across 162 delivered loads, with 87 of them late. The next-worst is Redline Carriers 62 LLC at 83.89%, so Bluegrass is a clear outlier.
sql:
WITH d AS (
  SELECT l.carrier_id,
         COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
         SUM(CASE WHEN l.delivery_actual > l.delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_loads
  FROM loads l
  WHERE l.status = 'Delivered'
  GROUP BY l.carrier_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50
)
SELECT c.name AS carrier,
       d.delivered_loads,
       d.late_loads,
       ROUND(100.0 * (d.delivered_loads - d.late_loads) / d.delivered_loads, 2) AS on_time_pct
FROM d
JOIN carriers c ON c.carrier_id = d.carrier_id
ORDER BY on_time_pct ASC, d.delivered_loads DESC
LIMIT 5
